recognize_zh: 周邊血液中的異常細胞核呈雙葉、左右對稱的蝴蝶／滑板狀（bilobed, butterfly nucleus），胞質淡灰藍、顆粒極細幾乎看不到，血小板稀少，這是微顆粒型急性前骨髓細胞白血病（APL, microgranular variant）的典型線索。
features: Abnormal promyelocyte with a bilobed, overlapping butterfly-shaped nucleus
Moderate pale gray-blue cytoplasm with very fine, barely visible granules (hypogranular)
Second cell with a round to subtly folded nucleus and finely granular violet cytoplasm
No Auer rod bundles visible; platelets very sparse in this field
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows scattered abnormal leukocytes, including a cell with a characteristic bilobed butterfly-shaped nucleus and pale gray-blue cytoplasm containing only very fine granules, and another cell with a round to slightly folded nucleus and finely granular cytoplasm. Auer rods are not seen in this field and platelets appear markedly decreased. Red cells are normocytic. Findings are suggestive of the microgranular (hypogranular) variant of acute promyelocytic leukemia; urgent coagulation studies and PML-RARA testing are recommended.

ddx.vs: Monocytic cells have folded nuclei with lacy chromatin and vacuolated cytoplasm and are NSE-positive, whereas microgranular APL cells are strongly MPO-positive, CD34/HLA-DR negative and PML-RARA positive.
Classic APL has cytoplasm filled with coarse azurophilic granules and faggot cells, while the microgranular variant appears nearly agranular by light microscopy and usually has higher WBC counts.
NPM1-mutated blasts can have cup-like nuclei and be HLA-DR/CD34 negative, but lack butterfly nuclei, DIC and PML-RARA fusion.
